title: Zephaniah Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Zephaniah chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Zephaniah Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Zephaniah Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who is called to gather themselves together in Zephaniah 2?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:1 calls "O nation not desired" to gather themselves together.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2, what should be sought by the meek of the earth?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:3 instructs the meek of the earth to seek righteousness and meekness.

questions.question: Which city is said to be forsaken in Zephaniah 2?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:4 states that Gaza shall be forsaken.

questions.question: What will happen to Ashkelon according to Zephaniah 2?
options: It shall be a strong fortress
It shall be a place of worship
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:4 declares that Ashkelon shall be a desolation.

questions.question: Who are the inhabitants of the sea coast addressed in Zephaniah 2:5?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:5 mentions the inhabitants of the sea coast as the nation of the Cherethites.

questions.question: True or False: Zephaniah 2:2 warns before the decree bring forth and before the day of the LORD'S anger come upon you.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:2 warns to act before the decree is brought forth and before the day of the LORD's anger comes.

questions.question: Which city will be rooted up according to Zephaniah 2?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:4 states that Ekron shall be rooted up.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2:1, the nation is described as what?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:1 describes the nation as "not desired."

questions.question: True or False: Zephaniah 2:3 says seeking the LORD may hide you in the day of the LORD'S anger.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:3 says it may be you shall be hid in the day of the LORD's anger if you seek the LORD.

questions.question: What will happen to Ashdod at noonday according to Zephaniah 2?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:4 says they shall drive out Ashdod at the noonday.

questions.question: True or False: According to Zephaniah 2:5, the land of the Philistines will be preserved and inhabited.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:5 states the land of the Philistines will be destroyed so there shall be no inhabitant.

questions.question: In Zephaniah 2, what comes first?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:1 commands gathering together before the other events described later in the chapter.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Zephaniah 2:5 for the LORD's word against the inhabitants of the sea coast?
options: Because they are Cherethites and the land of the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are Cherethites and the land of the Philistines
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:5 identifies the nation of Cherethites and the land of the Philistines as those against whom the word of the LORD is spoken.

questions.question: Who does Zephaniah 2 call to seek the LORD?
options: All ye meek of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: All ye meek of the earth
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:3 calls "all ye meek of the earth" to seek the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Zephaniah 2:2 warns that the day of the LORD'S anger will come after the day passes as the chaff.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:2 says the day will pass as the chaff before the day of the LORD'S anger comes, meaning the anger comes before the day passes as chaff.

medium.title: Zephaniah Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Zephaniah Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2:6, what will the sea coast become?
options: Dwellings and cottages for shepherds, and folds for flocks
A great city filled with merchants
questions.correctAnswer: Dwellings and cottages for shepherds, and folds for flocks
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:6 explicitly states that the sea coast shall become dwellings and cottages for shepherds, and folds for flocks, indicating a transformation from a populated area to one used for pastoral purposes.

questions.question: Who will inhabit the coast according to Zephaniah 2:7?
options: The remnant of the house of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The remnant of the house of Judah
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:7 reveals that the remnant of the house of Judah will inhabit the coast, feeding there and lying down in the houses of Ashkelon because the LORD will visit them and turn away their captivity.

questions.question: What reason does Zephaniah 2:8 give for God's judgment on Moab and Ammon?
options: They have reproached and magnified themselves against God's people
They have stolen from the house of Judah
They have worshipped idols in secret
questions.correctAnswer: They have reproached and magnified themselves against God's people
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:8 says God has heard the reproach of Moab and the revilings of the children of Ammon against His people, showing that their pride and opposition to God's people is the cause of judgment.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2:9, what will Moab and the children of Ammon become?
options: Like Sodom and Gomorrah, a perpetual desolation
A place of refuge for the poor
A land of great harvests and peace
questions.correctAnswer: Like Sodom and Gomorrah, a perpetual desolation
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:9 declares that Moab shall be like Sodom and Ammon like Gomorrah, becoming nettles, saltpits, and perpetual desolation, as punishment for their pride and reproach against God's people.

questions.question: What consequence does Zephaniah 2:10 say Moab and Ammon will receive for their pride?
options: They will be punished because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the LORD
They will be rewarded for their strength
They will become leaders among the nations
They will be forgotten and ignored
questions.correctAnswer: They will be punished because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the LORD
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:10 explains the reason for their punishment is their pride and the way they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the LORD of hosts.

questions.question: How does Zephaniah 2:7 teach about God's faithfulness to His people?
options: God will visit the remnant of Judah and turn away their captivity
God will abandon His people to their enemies
God will punish the remnant severely
God will give riches to the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: God will visit the remnant of Judah and turn away their captivity
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:7 promises that the LORD their God will visit the remnant of Judah and turn away their captivity, showing God's faithfulness and care for His obedient people.

questions.question: What practical lesson about humility can be learned from the punishment of Moab and Ammon in Zephaniah 2:9-10?
options: Pride and magnifying oneself against God's people leads to desolation
Ignoring others' reproach leads to strength
questions.correctAnswer: Pride and magnifying oneself against God's people leads to desolation
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:9-10 teach that pride and magnifying oneself against God's people leads to destruction and desolation, encouraging humility and respect for God's people.

questions.question: What does Zephaniah 2:6-7 imply about God's plan for the land and His people?
options: God will restore the land as a place for His people to dwell and feed
God will leave the land empty and desolate
God will give the land to foreign nations permanently
God will destroy the land completely
questions.correctAnswer: God will restore the land as a place for His people to dwell and feed
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 together show that while the land will be desolate for some, the coast will become dwellings for shepherds and the remnant of Judah will feed there, indicating restoration and provision by God.

questions.question: Based on Zephaniah 2:8-10, what biblical truth applies when a fellow believer experiences slander or reproach from others?
options: God hears the reproach and will act justly against those who magnify themselves against His people
God ignores the insults against His people
Believers should isolate themselves from others
questions.correctAnswer: God hears the reproach and will act justly against those who magnify themselves against His people
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:8-10 teaches that God hears when His people are reproached and magnified against, and He will bring judgment on those who act pridefully, encouraging believers to trust God's justice.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2:7, what is the significance of the inhabitants lying down in the houses of Ashkelon in the evening?
options: It signifies God’s restoration and turning away of captivity for the remnant of Judah
It shows they are captive prisoners
It indicates they have become Philistines
It reflects their defeat in battle
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies God’s restoration and turning away of captivity for the remnant of Judah
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:7 states that the remnant of Judah will lie down in the houses of Ashkelon because the LORD will visit them and turn away their captivity, symbolizing restoration and peace.

questions.question: True or False: Zephaniah 2:6 teaches that the sea coast will become a place of desolation with no life.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:6 says the sea coast shall be dwellings and cottages for shepherds and folds for flocks, indicating habitation and pastoral life, not desolation.

questions.question: True or False: Zephaniah 2:10 states that pride is the cause of God's judgment on those who reproach His people.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:10 clearly states that the punishment is because of their pride in reproaching and magnifying themselves against the people of the LORD of hosts.

questions.question: What does Zephaniah 2:9 suggest will happen to the residue and remnant of God's people after Moab and Ammon are desolated?
options: They shall spoil and possess Moab and Ammon
They will flee to other nations
They will be destroyed alongside Moab and Ammon
They will be enslaved by Moab and Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: They shall spoil and possess Moab and Ammon
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:9 states that the residue and remnant of God's people will spoil and possess the land of Moab and Ammon after they become desolate.

questions.question: True or False: According to Zephaniah 2:7, God promises to turn away the captivity of the remnant of Judah.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:7 clearly promises that the LORD their God shall visit the remnant of Judah and turn away their captivity.

questions.question: How does Zephaniah 2:8-10 teach about God’s justice in response to insults against His people?
options: God will punish those who magnify themselves against His people
God will cause His people to flee
questions.correctAnswer: God will punish those who magnify themselves against His people
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 show that God hears the reproach of Moab and Ammon and will punish them for their pride and magnification against His people, demonstrating His justice.

hard.title: Zephaniah Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Zephaniah Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2:11, what will the LORD do to the gods of the earth?
options: He will destroy all the gods by fire
He will famish all the gods of the earth
He will bless the gods to guide men
questions.correctAnswer: He will famish all the gods of the earth
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:11 states that the LORD will famish all the gods of the earth, indicating the LORD's supremacy and judgment over all false gods.

questions.question: What fate is declared for the Ethiopians in Zephaniah 2:12?
options: They shall be blessed and prosper
They shall be slain by the sword of the LORD
They shall be given new land
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be slain by the sword of the LORD
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:12 explicitly states that the Ethiopians will be slain by the LORD's sword, indicating divine judgment upon them.

questions.question: Which city is described as becoming a desolation and dry like a wilderness in Zephaniah 2:13?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:13 indicates that Assyria will be destroyed and Nineveh will become a desolation, dry like a wilderness, symbolizing the fall of a great city.

questions.question: In Zephaniah 2:14, which birds are said to lodge in the upper lintels of Nineveh?
questions.explanation: The verse depicts desolation through imagery of cormorant and bittern lodging in the upper lintels, symbolic of abandonment and ruin.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Zephaniah 2:15 when describing Nineveh as 'the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly'?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:15 uses irony by calling Nineveh a 'rejoicing city' that dwelt carelessly, yet it becomes a desolation, highlighting the contrast between pride and downfall.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'famish' in Zephaniah 2:11?
options: To cause extreme hunger or starvation
questions.correctAnswer: To cause extreme hunger or starvation
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'raḥav' used for 'famish' implies causing severe hunger or starvation, emphasizing the LORD's power to deprive false gods of power.

questions.question: Which northern empire does Zephaniah prophesy will be destroyed?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:13 states that the LORD will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria, indicating the fall of this dominant empire.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2:8-10, why will Moab and Ammon face desolation?
options: Because they allied with Israel's enemies
Because they reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the LORD
Because they refused to pay tribute
questions.correctAnswer: Because they reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 declare that Moab and Ammon face desolation due to their pride and reproach against Israel, God's people.

questions.question: True or False: Zephaniah 2:7 promises that the remnant of Judah will find refuge in the houses of Ashkelon.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:7 says the remnant of Judah will feed and lie down in the houses of Ashkelon, showing God's restoration and visitation of His people.

questions.question: Zephaniah 2:6 states what the sea coast will become after judgment. What is it?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 describes the sea coast becoming places for shepherds and flocks, indicating a complete change in use after judgment upon the Philistines.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of the LORD's judgment on false gods as found in Zephaniah 2:11?
questions.explanation: Psalm 96:5 echoes the theme by declaring that all gods are idols, but the LORD made the heavens, emphasizing His supremacy over false gods like in Zephaniah 2:11.

questions.question: Zephaniah 2:15 refers to Nineveh as a 'rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly.' Which New Testament passage reflects a similar theme of pride leading to ruin?
questions.explanation: Revelation 18 describes Babylon as a proud city that falls into desolation, paralleling Nineveh's careless pride and downfall in Zephaniah 2:15.

questions.question: What historical context helps explain the prophecy against Assyria and Nineveh in Zephaniah 2:13-15?
options: Assyrian empire's dominance and cruelty before its fall
questions.correctAnswer: Assyrian empire's dominance and cruelty before its fall
questions.explanation: Zephaniah prophesies against Assyria and Nineveh, reflecting their historical role as a dominant and oppressive empire prior to destruction.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'the day of the LORD'S anger' appears in Zephaniah 2:2 and calls for repentance before judgment.
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:2 warns to seek the LORD before the day of His fierce anger comes, urging repentance before judgment.

questions.question: How does Zephaniah 2:3 describe those who might be hidden on the day of the LORD'S anger?
options: The meek of the earth who seek righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The meek of the earth who seek righteousness
questions.explanation: Verse 3 advises the meek who seek righteousness and meekness may be hidden during the LORD's anger, underscoring humility as a protective trait.

theological.title: Zephaniah Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Zephaniah Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Zephaniah 2:1 urge the people to do?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:1 explicitly calls for the nation to gather themselves together, emphasizing the need for unity in response to impending judgment.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2:3, who should seek the LORD?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:3 highlights that it is the meek of the earth who have wrought His judgment and are encouraged to seek righteousness and meekness.

questions.question: What fate does Zephaniah 2:5 declare for Canaan, the land of the Philistines?
questions.explanation: In Zephaniah 2:5, the LORD declares that Canaan will be destroyed, indicating God's judgment on the inhabitants for their sins.

questions.question: What does Zephaniah 2:7 promise for the remnant of the house of Judah?
options: They shall feed and lie down in safety
questions.correctAnswer: They shall feed and lie down in safety
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:7 assures that the remnant of the house of Judah will find sustenance and safety, as the LORD will visit and restore them.

questions.question: What does Zephaniah 2:10 say shall happen to Moab and Ammon?
questions.explanation: According to Zephaniah 2:10, Moab and Ammon will face destruction as a consequence of their pride and reproach against the people of the LORD.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Zephaniah 2:11 regarding His relationship with the nations?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:11 reveals God's judgment as He will famish all the gods of the earth, indicating His sovereignty over all nations and idols.

questions.question: What does Zephaniah 2:13 say about the fate of Assyria?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:13 proclaims that Assyria will be destroyed and made desolate, demonstrating God's judgment against nations opposing Him.

questions.question: Zephaniah 2:15 describes a city that dwelt carelessly. Which city is referred to?
questions.explanation: The description in Zephaniah 2:15 fits Nineveh, which was known for its pride and carelessness, resulting in its eventual desolation.

questions.question: How does Zephaniah 2:4 contribute to the understanding of divine judgment?
options: It specifies the places under judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It specifies the places under judgment
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:4 specifically mentions Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, and Ekron, showing that these locations are under divine judgment.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Zephaniah 2:9 for the pride of Moab and Ammon?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:9 states the consequence of their pride is desolation, comparing them to Sodom and Gomorrah as a warning of judgment.

questions.question: What does Zephaniah 2:6 suggest will happen to the sea coast?
options: It will be a place for shepherds
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a place for shepherds
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:6 indicates that the sea coast will become dwellings and cottages for shepherds, symbolizing a restoration following judgment.

questions.question: According to Zephaniah 2:12, what fate awaits the Ethiopians?
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:12 states a clear judgment against the Ethiopians, indicating that they too will face destruction by the sword.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Zephaniah 2:1-3 convey about repentance?
options: Gathering and seeking the LORD is essential
questions.correctAnswer: Gathering and seeking the LORD is essential
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:1-3 collectively emphasize the call to gather and seek the LORD, presenting repentance as a necessary response to impending judgment.

questions.question: What combined theme can be drawn from Zephaniah 2:8-10 regarding pride?
options: Pride results in judgment and desolation
questions.correctAnswer: Pride results in judgment and desolation
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:8-10 shows that the pride of Moab and Ammon leads to their judgment, emphasizing that pride incurs divine wrath.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's sovereignty can be derived from Zephaniah 2:11-13?
options: God exercises sovereignty over all nations
God is only concerned with Israel
God does not judge the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: God exercises sovereignty over all nations
questions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:11-13 illustrates God's sovereignty as He declares judgment against Assyria and the nations, reinforcing His authority over all.
